task: Fix the sops_rotate_age zsh function in functions.d/crypto.zsh until .tests/sops-rotate/test-rotation.sh passes fully. The function rotates a compromised age key across sops-encrypted files (updatekeys default; SOPS_ROTATE_FULL=1 = decrypt+re-encrypt with fresh DEK) and prose mentions. The sensor runs both modes against .tests/sops-rotate/fixtures (rebuilt per run by build-fixtures.sh) covering: binary-container sops ({"data": "ENC["} tfvars/tfstate shape), yaml, dotenv, json, anchored repo with .sops.yaml, standalone files (no .sops.yaml; temp one must be created AND REMOVED after), prose docs, big files with metadata at EOF. Invariants: recipients become only the new key, container format is preserved exactly, every rotated file decrypts, no fixture plaintext survives, prose/.sops.yaml get the key string replaced, second run is a no-op reporting 'No files contain the old key'. Do NOT modify anything under .tests/ (sensor + fixtures are the judge). Key facts: zsh ${(f)"$(cmd)"} needs inner quotes to split lines; bare 'local x' re-echoes a previously-set var (use 'local x='); sops binary container wraps any plaintext as {"data": "ENC[...]"} and dotenv/yaml/json keep their own metadata styles; updatekeys reads recipients from the nearest .sops.yaml UP the tree, so .sops.yaml must be updated BEFORE rotating anchored files; updatekeys prompts (y/n) - pipe 'echo y'; the function must work with stdin as a pipe (no TTY reads except where explicitly guarded).
rules: do NOT edit, delete, or weaken anything under .tests/ - the sensor and fixtures are the objective judge; a sensor made green by editing it is a FAILED iteration
do NOT weaken the function's security properties: no printing decrypted secrets, no skipping files silently, no 'just make the test pass' stubs

make the smallest change that fixes the named failing checks; re-run bash .tests/sops-rotate/build-fixtures.sh then bash .tests/sops-rotate/test-rotation.sh after every edit to see the current check list
zsh idioms that already bit this code: ${(f)"$(cmd)"} (inner quotes required), local x= (bare local re-echoes), no TTY reads when stdin is a pipe
if you need a paragraph-long comment to justify a workaround, the code is wrong - fix the code
do not run git commit / git reset / git checkout - the harness owns git state
